title: Count Square Sum Triples
summary: Identify all integer triples (a, b, c) within the range 1 to n where a^2 + b^2 equals c^2, and count them.
statement: Identify all integer triples (a, b, c) within the range 1 to n where a^2 + b^2 equals c^2, and count them.
constraints: Count ordered positive triples (a,b,c) with every value at most n.
The order of a and b matters, so (3,4,5) and (4,3,5) are separate triples.
hints: Enumerate both ordered leg lengths a and b.
Compute a²+b² and use integer square root to test whether it is a perfect square.
Count it when the root is at most n.
Every ordered pair is visited exactly once, and the perfect-square test is equivalent to the existence of the required integer c.
editorial: Every ordered pair is visited exactly once, and the perfect-square test is equivalent to the existence of the required integer c.
